$comment: The gateway route table for the edge VM (ADR-0012 §1, ADR-0013 §5). Mounted at
/opt/opsgrids/routes.prod.json and selected with ROUTES_FILE.
It is a separate file from services/app-gateway/routes.json rather than an edit to it,
for two reasons. Every upstream in the committed table is http://localhost:<port>, which
is correct for `make run` and meaningless inside a container. And only the services in
compose.prod.yml are deployed — a prefix pointing at a service that is not running is a
hung connection and a 504, where a prefix that is absent is an immediate 404 from the
gateway that names the path. A 404 for a product nobody deployed is the honest answer.
The semantics are the committed table's, unchanged: longest prefix wins, `product` names
the entitlement a request needs, and the storefront pair is split so the anonymous buyer
surface carries no `product` key. A prefix here does not make anything public — the
public paths are an exact-match frozenset in the gateway's own app/main.py.
Prefixes are the services' REAL mounted paths (`create_app` mounts every router at
/api/v1 with no per-service segment): billing's routes are /api/v1/invoices and
/api/v1/credit-balance, not /api/v1/billing/…; the committed table reaches only billing's
info route and that is a defect there, not a convention to copy.
A prefix for a service behind a compose profile (operations → `inventory`) is present
whether or not the profile is enabled: preflight refuses to deploy when the catalogue
sells a product whose profile is off, so the 504 that would otherwise result cannot
reach a customer.
When a service is added to compose.prod.yml, it is added here. When a route is added to
the committed table for a service that is deployed, it must be added here too — nothing
checks that for you, and the symptom is a 404 on a route that works locally.
`/api/v1/auth/operator` is `blocked`, mirroring services/app-gateway/routes.json exactly —
longer than the `/api/v1/auth` entry below, so it wins the match for every operator
sign-in path here too and is refused with 404 before any token is decoded. Operator
traffic reaches auth only through admin-gateway; tests/infra checks every blocked entry
in the dev table has an identical one here.
`/api/v1/webhooks/whatsapp` is Meta's callback. It carries no bearer token, so it is ALSO
declared in the gateway's `WEBHOOK_PUBLIC_PATHS` (services/app-gateway/app/main.py), by
exact path and method (GET handshake, POST delivery) — a route here that the gateway does
not declare answers every delivery with 401. Its `max_body_bytes` is 3 MiB, Meta's
documented payload ceiling, rather than the 2 MiB default. tests/infra/
test_route_table_parity.py fails when this entry, the dev table, the policy or that cap
drift apart. `/api/v1/webhooks/razorpay` is routed but deliberately NOT public in the
gateway yet; that is a separate decision.
The three `/api/v1/webhooks/whatsapp/deauthorize|data-deletion|data-deletion-status`
entries are Facebook Login's deauthorize and data-deletion callbacks — see the matching
comment in services/app-gateway/routes.json. Same upstream as the rest of notification,
own small `max_body_bytes`, also declared in `WEBHOOK_PUBLIC_PATHS`.
`/api/v1/webhooks/razorpay/collections` is a *tenant's* Razorpay webhook (tenant payment
collection, ADR-0024 §8) — distinct from the platform's own `/api/v1/webhooks/razorpay`,
which stays routed-but-not-public. Declared public in `WEBHOOK_PUBLIC_PATHS` for POST only;
payment verifies each body against that merchant's own sealed webhook secret, named by the
`?account=` query. 256 KiB cap, the same ceiling payment enforces behind it.
`/api/v1/webhooks/collections` is the provider-neutral path to the same handler (ADR-0033):
Cashfree merchants register it and Cashfree Orders name it as `notify_url`. Public in
`WEBHOOK_PUBLIC_PATHS` for POST only, the same 256 KiB cap; payment takes the provider from
the account row, never from the path.
